questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Cape Verde?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Cape Verde article.

questions.proof: The city suffered several pirate raids and for this reason in 1712, after a French attack, the authorities were forced to move the capital to Praia, where it is located until now.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Praia?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Cape Verde is Praia.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Cape Verde about 4,033 square kilometres; Mauritius about 2,040 square kilometres; São Tomé and Príncipe about 1,001 square kilometres; Seychelles about 459 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Cape Verde?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Economy” part of the Cape Verde article.

questions.proof: The national currency is the Cape Verdean escudo.

questions.prompt: Which continent is Cape Verde in?

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Cape Verde on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Cape Verde on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
